newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria cenbank declines comment on gold reserves.
newsitem.headline: Austria cenbank declines comment on gold reserves.

text.p: The Austrian National Bank declined to comment on Friday on whether or not there were plans to revalue Austrian gold reserves in line with German proposals to revalue the Bundesbank's gold reserves.
"We can't comment on that," a spokesman told Reuters.
Austrian gold reserves were valued in the central bank's books at 18.98 billion schillings at the end of April, down from 19.6 billion at the end of last year.
The bank has some 316 tons of gold in its vaults, which it values at 60,000 schillings per kilo. The current market price is at around 133,000 schillings per kilo.
Some 100 additional tons of gold have been sold by the central bank on a swap basis. "They will come back to us at some point," the spokesman said.
He added the valuation method had last been changed at the end of 1979, when the gold's book value was raised from 45,000 schillings per kilo.

German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said this week he wanted Bundesbank gold and currency reserves to be revalued from current low book prices to levels closer to the going market price in a bid to plug a growing hole in state accounts. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 274
